pins.name: SCL
pins.label: SCL (GPIO0)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. No onboard user button on this board (checked - see notes.txt)

pins.name: P4
pins.label: P4 (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: SDA
pins.label: SDA (GPIO2)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. Commonly wired to the on-board LED on dev boards

pins.name: P3
pins.label: P3 (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: P1
pins.label: GPIO5 (Led active high)
pins.notes:
Onboard user LED (active-high, LED_BUILTIN) - confirmed via official schematic, see chipGpios note
Onboard user LED (active-high) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: SS
pins.label: SS (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: P10
pins.label: P10 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Oak has an on-board resistor-divider giving A0 a 0-3.2V range (unlike the bare chip's native 0-1.0V) - see adc note below
